discoveredAssets: localhost:8000 - Flask-based CAPTCHA User Registration Application (Python 3.13, Werkzeug 3.1.3) - Port 8000

targets.objective: Test for CAPTCHA padding oracle vulnerability via AES-256 encryption, assess CSRF token implementation, test for cookie manipulation, brute force encrypted CAPTCHA values, validate session management security, and test for authentication bypass or privilege escalation
targets.rationale: Primary application endpoint implementing CAPTCHA validation with encrypted cookie storage using AES-256-CBC with hardcoded key and PKCS7 padding. This is the main entry point and implements user registration. The encryption scheme appears vulnerable to padding oracle attacks based on the application's error handling that distinguishes between different failure modes

keyFindings: [HIGH] Flask application running on port 8000 with CAPTCHA protection using AES-256 encryption for cookie storage
[HIGH] Hardcoded AES encryption key visible in application source code: 'C'*32
[HIGH] CAPTCHA implementation only displays 8 of 14 characters on image, requiring users to guess last 6 characters
[HIGH] Application uses CSRF tokens for POST request protection - Flask-WTF properly implemented
[HIGH] Encrypted cookies (base64-encoded IV + ciphertext) stored as 'captcha' cookie containing CAPTCHA validation data
[MEDIUM] Single endpoint (/) handling both GET (display form) and POST (validate CAPTCHA) operations
[MEDIUM] Session management uses Flask secure session cookies with HttpOnly flag set
[MEDIUM] No API documentation endpoints or debug interfaces exposed (robots.txt, swagger.json, openapi.json, etc. return 404)
[MEDIUM] Error responses may leak information about padding validation - potential padding oracle exploitation surface
[LOW] No directory listing, backup files, or configuration files exposed
[LOW] Application properly implements Werkzeug/Flask security headers for session management
